--- title: "[Graph.degree_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate degree centrality scores for all nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40003-L40110){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.degree_centrality( mode="all", attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Degree centrality](/assets/graphs/degree-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by degree centrality, each degree divided by n - 1 = 6. Hub C touches four of the six other nodes and tops the table at 0.67, followed by B, D and E at 0.50, A and F at 0.33, and the pendant node G at 0.17." width="100%"} Degree centrality is a node's degree divided by `n - 1`, the largest degree any node can have in a simple graph with `n` nodes. A score of `1` means the node is adjacent to every other node; `0` means it is isolated. Dividing by `n - 1` makes scores comparable across graphs of different sizes, which raw degrees from `degrees()` are not. In directed graphs, `mode=` chooses which edges count: incoming edges (in-degree centrality, often read as popularity or prestige), outgoing edges (out-degree centrality, often read as activity or influence), or both. A self-loop adds `2` to a node's total degree, and parallel edges each count, so scores can exceed `1` on graphs that are not simple. This matches NetworkX's `degree_centrality()`, `in_degree_centrality()`, and `out_degree_centrality()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["all"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which degree to use in directed graphs where: (1) `"all"` counts incoming and outgoing edges (default), (2) `"in"` counts incoming edges only, and (3) `"out"` counts outgoing edges only. Ignored for undirected graphs. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store degree centrality scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `"degree_centrality"`. Overwrites the column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to degree centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The hub of a star is adjacent to every other node, so its degree centrality is `1`; each leaf touches one of the four other nodes and scores `0.25`: ::: {#d49459c0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["Hub", "A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("Hub", "A"), ("Hub", "B"), ("Hub", "C"), ("Hub", "D")]) ) scores = graph.degree_centrality(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): score for nid, score in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'Hub': 1.0, 'A': 0.25, 'B': 0.25, 'C': 0.25, 'D': 0.25} ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph, in-degree and out-degree centrality can rank nodes very differently. Here everyone follows "Celebrity", who follows no one back: ::: {#1d3cd6f9 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["Celebrity", "Fan1", "Fan2", "Fan3"]) .add_edges([("Fan1", "Celebrity"), ("Fan2", "Celebrity"), ("Fan3", "Celebrity")]) .add_edge("Fan1", "Fan2") .degree_centrality(mode="in", attr_name="in_deg") .degree_centrality(mode="out", attr_name="out_deg") ) graph.get_node_df().select(["label", "in_deg", "out_deg"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
